applicability.rationale: The report describes individual assignment of patients to dapagliflozin or matching placebo using a sequestered fixed randomization schedule.

result.relation_rationale: The reported primary composite uses the requested event set and definition, compares randomized dapagliflozin with placebo, and estimates the treatment effect from randomization over trial follow-up (median 18.2 months). All randomized participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis; incomplete primary-outcome follow-up is separately reported.

Investigators used an interactive voice- or Web-
response system to determine treatment assign-
ment. Randomization was stratified on the basis
of a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes (i.e., an estab-
lished diagnosis or a glycated hemoglobin level
of ≥6.5% [≥48 mmol per mole]) confirmed at
screening.
Patients were evaluated at 14 days and 60 days
after randomization, with a focus on assessment
of heart failure and volume status, adverse events,
and an evaluation of renal function and potassi-
um levels. Additional trial visits were scheduled
at 4 months and at 4-month intervals thereafter
(Fig. S1 in the Supplementary Appendix, avail-
able at NEJM.org). The full schedule of assess-
ments is provided in the trial protocol. Dapa-
gliflozin or placebo was to be discontinued if
pregnancy or diabetic ketoacidosis occurred. Dose
reduction (to 5 mg daily of dapagliflozin or pla-
cebo) or temporary discontinuation was permitted
in case of an acute, unexpected decline in the
eGFR, volume depletion, or hypotension (or to
avoid these conditions), with a subsequent increase
in dose or restarting of treatment, if possible.
Outcomes
The primary outcome was a composite of wors-
ening heart failure or death from cardiovascular
causes. An episode of worsening heart failure
was either an unplanned hospitalization or an

heart failure.

hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular

answers.justification: The randomized groups were 2373 and 2371. The outcome flow reports incomplete primary-outcome follow-up for 14 dapagliflozin and 20 placebo participants, plus two placebo participants with unknown vital status. Even counting the two unknown statuses separately, fewer than 1% of randomized participants lacked complete outcome follow-up. Given this small fraction and the common primary event (386 and 502 events), outcome data were probably available for nearly all randomized participants. The diagram does not establish whether the two unknown vital statuses overlap with the 20 incomplete-follow-up count.
unknowns: The report does not clarify whether the two placebo participants with unknown vital status are included among the 20 with incomplete primary-outcome follow-up.

development_oct2.requested_outcome: Composite of worsening heart failure (hospitalization or urgent visit with IV therapy) or cardiovascular death

applicability.rationale: 4744 patients were randomly assigned in two parallel groups.

result.relation_rationale: The reported primary outcome matches the requested event set: cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, or urgent visit resulting in IV therapy for heart failure, from randomization, in all randomized patients assigned to dapagliflozin or placebo. Follow-up median was 18.2 months. The main estimate is the time-to-first-event hazard ratio.

The primary composite outcome of worsening
heart failure (hospitalization or an urgent visit
resulting in intravenous therapy for heart failure)
or death from cardiovascular causes occurred in
386 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group
and in 502 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group
(hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI],

answers.justification: The participant-flow figure reports 14 of 2373 dapagliflozin participants and 20 of 2371 placebo participants with incomplete follow-up for the primary outcome. The adjacent primary-result passage reports 386 and 502 primary composite events. The incomplete follow-up counts are less than 1% in each arm, supporting outcome data availability for nearly all randomized participants. The figure also records two placebo participants with unknown vital status, without clarifying whether these overlap the 20 with incomplete primary-outcome follow-up; they are not counted separately.
